Review.ItemLabel: Compile-emitter check: WAIT FOR ACTIONS QUIET emits WaitForQuietAsync
Review.Feedback: This compile-only smoke uses NAVIGATE TO + WAIT FOR ACTIONS QUIET (no label probes) so it bypasses the W0 SemanticValidator's role='*' limitation that blocks any catalog-grounded checklist from compiling without W0 CLI --suppressions support. The emitter's output still shows TWO WaitForQuietAsync calls because the existing EmitWatermarkWaits flag emits one implicitly after NAVIGATE TO and the new explicit verb emits the second; this is the transitional-debt coexistence that Session 2's verifier flagged for follow-up. The point being proven here is just that the explicit verb resolves to the C# helper end-to-end; production usage of the verb pairs it with an interaction step (see HR#8 in the uat-script-author prompt template).
